skill.name: golang-samber-oops
skill.description: Structured error handling in Golang with samber/oops — error builders, stack traces, error codes, error context, error wrapping, error attributes, user-facing vs developer messages, panic recovery, and logger integration. Apply when using or adopting samber/oops, or when the codebase already imports github.com/samber/oops.
skill.summary: Build structured Go errors with samber/oops, preserve context across layers, and separate public messages from diagnostic details.
skill.author: samber

security_audit.summary: All 66 static findings are false positives involving documentation formatting, Go identifiers, example SQL, tool declarations, or reference URLs. No evidence found of malicious commands, credential theft, unauthorized network transfers, or audit-directed prompt injection. One semantic risk remains: examples propagate email addresses and raw input into errors that can be logged without redaction guidance.

remediation.issue: Examples attach email addresses and raw input to structured errors without explaining redaction before logging.
remediation.suggestion: Use synthetic or minimized identifiers, redact sensitive attributes before logging, and document an allowlist for request metadata and input fields.

content.user_title: Build Structured Go Errors with samber/oops
content.value_statement: Plain Go errors can lose diagnostic context and produce inconsistent public messages. This skill guides structured error creation, wrapping, context propagation, and logging with samber/oops.
actual_capabilities: Guide fluent error builders with domains, tags, machine-readable codes, and structured attributes.
Explain nil-safe wrapping and contextual error enrichment across application layers.
Separate public error messages from technical details using Public and GetPublic.
Demonstrate reusable builders and middleware context propagation with WithBuilder and FromContext.
Show panic recovery, invariant assertions, and structured error field inspection.
Provide stack trace configuration and logging examples for slog, zerolog, and logrus.
limitations: Provides instructions and examples, not a standalone Go runtime or automatic error-handling service.
Examples require adaptation, dependency setup, and testing against the installed samber/oops version.
Package navigation and documentation lookup depend on separately available tools or related skills.
Does not provide automatic redaction; review attached user data, request metadata, and raw inputs before logging.

use_cases.title: Improve API Error Responses
use_cases.description: Separate stable public messages from detailed repository and service errors while retaining request context for debugging.

use_cases.title: Standardize Operational Diagnostics
use_cases.description: Define domains, codes, tags, and stable messages so errors remain useful across layers and easier to group in monitoring.

use_cases.title: Review Multi-Tenant Error Context
use_cases.description: Review reusable user and tenant builders, context propagation, and safe attribute selection across shared services.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Structured Error
prompt_templates.prompt: Show a basic samber/oops error for a failed order lookup. Add a domain, error code, and synthetic order identifier without interpolating identifiers into the message.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: learn the fluent builder pattern.

prompt_templates.title: Simplify Error Wrapping
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Go function using samber/oops: [paste function]. Simplify nil-safe wrapping and preserve the original error. Keep messages stable and exclude sensitive attributes.

prompt_templates.title: Propagate Context Across Layers
prompt_templates.prompt: Design samber/oops middleware and handler, service, and repository error handling. Propagate a trace identifier with WithBuilder and FromContext. Separate public messages and allowlisted diagnostic attributes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: align error context across an HTTP service.

prompt_templates.title: Review Recovery and Logging
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these worker and logging paths: [paste code]. Recommend samber/oops recovery boundaries, reusable builders, and stack trace settings. Identify sensitive attributes and propose redaction before logging.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: review operational safety across worker boundaries.

output_examples.input: An order failure needs diagnostic identifiers without creating a different message for every order.
output: Use the stable technical message: order processing failed.
Set the domain to order-service and the code to order_processing_failed.
Attach only approved order and tenant identifiers as structured attributes.
Keep variable identifiers out of the message so monitoring can group matching failures.

output_examples.input: A purchase fails because stock is insufficient. The API needs a safe message and useful internal diagnostics.
output: Return the public message: Not enough items in stock.
Use insufficient_stock as the machine-readable code.
Record requested and available quantities as diagnostic attributes.
Retrieve the public message with GetPublic and a generic fallback rather than returning the full technical error.

output_examples.input: Downstream handlers need the request trace identifier without adding more function parameters.
output: Create a base error builder in HTTP middleware with an approved trace identifier.
Store the builder in the request context using WithBuilder.
Retrieve it downstream with FromContext and add domain-specific tags or attributes.
Review request metadata before attaching it, even when body capture is disabled.

best_practices: Use stable messages and structured attributes, and verify examples against your installed library version.
Add relevant context at package boundaries while keeping public messages separate from technical details.
Allowlist diagnostic attributes and redact personal data, secrets, and request metadata before logging errors.
anti_patterns: Interpolating user, tenant, or order identifiers into messages that monitoring should group.
Returning full technical errors or stack traces directly to API consumers.
Copying examples that attach email addresses or raw inputs without reviewing log access and redaction.

faq.question: What does this skill provide?
faq.answer: It provides samber/oops instructions and Go examples for structured errors, wrapping, recovery, context propagation, and logger integration.

faq.question: Which tools and projects does it target?
faq.answer: It targets Codex and Claude Code workflows for Go projects using or adopting samber/oops.

faq.question: Does it install samber/oops automatically?
faq.answer: No. The skill provides guidance, and its declared installation list is empty. Set up project dependencies separately.

faq.question: Why keep identifiers outside error messages?
faq.answer: Stable messages support monitoring aggregation. Structured attributes retain approved diagnostic identifiers without producing a unique message for every failure.

faq.question: How are public and technical messages separated?
faq.answer: Use Public for a user-safe message and GetPublic with a fallback when responding. Keep technical details in restricted diagnostic logs.

faq.question: Are attached attributes automatically safe to log?
faq.answer: No. Review and redact email addresses, raw inputs, and request metadata before logging or forwarding errors to telemetry services.
